diagnostic_evidence.quote: By applying the triangle inequality and the lifting theorem (see~\cite[Sect. 6]{beirao2017stability}), we can write

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds |b-Pi b|_{1,K} by C|b-Pi b|_{1/2,dK}. A lifting theorem only controls the minimal-energy (harmonic) extension. Here w=b-Pi b has Laplacian in P_{kappa-2} and is not harmonic. The inequality is false on that class: any nonzero element of the bubble space has zero trace but positive H1 seminorm. The step is therefore unsupported as written. The statement is plausibly true: Pi is injective on bubbles, and a uniform scaling argument would then be needed, but no such argument is given.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove injectivity of Pi^nabla_kappa on the bubble space: Pi b=0 implies b is orthogonal to P_{kappa-2}, hence |b|_1^2=-int b Delta b=0. Combine this with a scaling/compactness argument under G1-G2 to get a uniform constant.
issues.overall_effect: The h-independent constant gamma_sharp is unproven. Stability of a_h (especially for beta_sharp=0, the choice used in the numerics), well-posedness and the error estimates rest on it.
issues.title: Lifting bound misapplied to non-harmonic function in bubble norm estimate
issues.why_classification: The statement survives, but the invalid step needs a contained replacement argument, including a uniform-in-shape constant. This is not a local fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: By applying the trace theorem and a scaling of boundary norms, we can write

issues.failure_explanation: Enhanced functions have Laplacian in P_k, so vtilde-Pi_k vtilde is not harmonic. Bounding its H1 seminorm by its H^{1/2} boundary seminorm is not a consequence of the trace or lifting theorem. On functions with polynomial Laplacian such a bound fails, since zero-trace members are nonzero. The key step toward the lower bound is therefore unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the step with a finite-dimensional argument. If (vtilde - Pi_k vtilde)=0 on dK, the enhancement constraint and Pi_k w=0 make w orthogonal to P_k, so |w|_1^2 = -int w Delta w = 0. Add a uniform scaling argument under G1-G2.
issues.overall_effect: The stability of the splitting v_h = vtilde + d_h is unproven.
issues.title: Same invalid lifting step for enhanced VEM functions in splitting stability
issues.why_classification: The result is recoverable, but only with a contained new argument, not a local edit.

issues.failure_explanation: Membership in the enhanced space of degree k+2 requires (v - Pi_{k+2} v, q)=0 for all q of degree k+1 and k+2. Elements of W~_k satisfy only the degree-k enhancement, and bubbles satisfy no such constraint. The claimed inclusion is therefore unsupported and false in general, and it is the only justification offered for the proposition.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Argue directly from the direct sum. dofs #1-#3 are unisolvent for W~_k, and moments of degree k-1, k are unisolvent for B_{k+2\k}.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the unisolvence proposition has no valid justification.
issues.title: False inclusion used to justify unisolvence of velocity dofs
issues.why_classification: A short direct argument restores the unchanged statement.

issues.failure_explanation: Adding and subtracting the cross term should give -2C* a(vtilde,d_h), not -a(Q_k vtilde,d_h). The term is then simply dropped as if nonpositive. Since a_h has no cross term, a_h(vtilde+d,.) equals a_h(vtilde-d,.), while a(Q_k vtilde,d) flips sign. So for one of the two choices the dropped term is positive, and the inference is invalid.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Bound a_h(v,v) <= C(|vtilde|_1^2+|d_h|_1^2) and apply the splitting stability of Prop. prop:added-3 to get a_h(v,v) <= C eta^{-2} a(v,v).
issues.overall_effect: The upper bound in eq:stab, and hence continuity of a_h, is not established by the given proof.
issues.title: Upper stability bound drops a sign-indefinite cross term
issues.why_classification: A short local repair using a result already in the paper preserves the statement, with a different constant.

issues.failure_explanation: By prop:norm_bub, B_{k+2\k} intersected with ker(Pi_{k+2}) is {0}, so the second line of eq:stab_ah imposes no condition on S_{k+2}. The proof nevertheless applies both S_{k+2} bounds to Q_{k+2} d_h = d_h - Pi_{k+2} d_h, which does not lie in that set (it is not in H^1_0 in general). This is used for the upper bound when beta_sharp>0 and for the lower bound when beta_sharp >= 1/gamma_star.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the S_{k+2} equivalence on (I - Pi_{k+2}) of the bubble space, or on a suitable superspace.
issues.overall_effect: For beta_sharp>0, stability of a_h is unsupported for any S_{k+2} satisfying the stated assumption. The case beta_sharp=0 is unaffected.
issues.title: Bubble stabilization assumption is vacuous and applied outside its domain
issues.why_classification: Correcting the domain of the assumption is local, and every claim survives.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper claims c_h is equivalent to the full L2 norm on Q_k. But c_h depends only on Q^0_k q_h. Any nonzero zero-mean global polynomial of degree k belongs to Q_k and gives c_h(q_h,q_h)=0, so the lower bound is false. Only the bound in terms of ||Q^0_k q_h|| follows from eq:stab_sp.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace ||q_h|| by ||Q^0_k q_h|| in both bounds.
issues.overall_effect: The claim misrepresents c_h as coercive on Q_k, which would trivialize the pressure stability. Later proofs use the correct Q^0_k version.
issues.title: False global norm equivalence for pressure stabilization c_h
issues.why_classification: The fix is a local restatement, and the arguments that follow already use the correct form.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Given a function $w\in\HunoK\cap C^0(\elementvem)$, we introduce the interpolant
For $v\in \mathrm{H}^{k+1}(\elementvem)$, the following optimal order error estimate holds true

issues.failure_explanation: v(q_h) is only in H^1_0, and in 2D H^1 functions need not be continuous, so the nodal interpolant is undefined. The proof then uses H1-stability and ||v-v_I||_0 <= Ch||v||_1, which are not provided: the paper's estimates require H^{k+1}. The same gap occurs for rho in H^1 (thm:added-3) and for p in H^k when deriving the rates (cor:added-1).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Introduce an H1-stable Clement/Scott-Zhang type quasi-interpolant into the enhanced VEM space that preserves moments up to k-2, with low-order estimates. Use it for v(q_h), rho and p.
issues.overall_effect: The weak inf-sup, and hence well-posedness and all error estimates, rely on unestablished low-regularity interpolation.
issues.title: Nodal interpolants applied to low-regularity functions without estimates
issues.why_classification: The repair needs a new interpolation lemma, but the results and rates are preserved.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For all $q_h\in Q_k$, there exists $\v_h\in\V_k$ with $\|\v_h\|_{1,\Omega}=\|q_h\|_{0,\Omega}$ such that

issues.failure_explanation: d_h is defined only through its moments. The proof never bounds |d_h|_1 in terms of ||v(q_h)||_1, yet the statement requires ||v_h||_1=||q_h||_0 for v_h=v_I+d_h. Without a bound such as |d_h|_{1,K} <= C h_K^{-1}||v-v_I||_{0,K}, which needs a norm equivalence between bubble moments and the H1 norm, normalizing v_h may destroy the h-independence of zeta_1.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove a scaled norm equivalence between bubble H1 norms and moment dofs under G1-G2. Use it to bound |d_h|_1 <= C|v(q_h)|_1, then renormalize v_h.
issues.overall_effect: The h-uniform weak inf-sup is not established, so the stability of B_h and the error estimates are unsupported.
issues.title: Bubble correction norm never bounded in weak inf-sup
issues.why_classification: The repair requires a contained new lemma, with no change to the method or rates.

issues.failure_explanation: a_h^K is defined through the splitting vtilde + bubble and through the dofs, which exist only on V_k(K). For u not in V_k(K), a_h^K(u_I-u,.) and a_h^K(u-Pi u,.) are undefined. Their continuity bounds, used later, are established only on V_k(K).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the standard splitting a_h(u_I - Pi u, v_h) + a(Pi u - u, v_h) + a(u, v_h) - a_h(u_h, v_h). Here u_I - Pi u lies in V_k(K), so eq:stab applies.
issues.overall_effect: The energy-error estimate is derived through undefined terms.
issues.title: Discrete form a_h applied to non-discrete exact solution
issues.why_classification: A routine local rewrite gives the same bound.
